@AitoLaikoSamoMoaCawfy  You are talking about pwm. A 555 with diodes can do it , it is a classical .  I mean changing the on/off ratio , the frequency is not important there. 
Dont forget a free wheel diode on the engine , if no , bye bye the mosfet.
Of course pwm is better.In fact a transistor (or mosfet) must be used 100 % open (low resistance) or closed once you can.
At 50 % ( Imax/2, Rengine=Rmosfet)  it is like a resistor and heat same as the engine. Without a radiator on this little thing , good luck.     

This video is for fun and show what a mosfet under 50 cents can do. It is impressive if you never did it.

text: Or a boost circuit works too. A buck converter converts higher voltage dc to lower voltage dc, boost converter converts low voltage dc to high voltage dc, and buck boost converter can convert a high or low voltage to a higher or lower voltage. Buck boost is required if supply(battery in your case) will provide a voltage within a certian number of volts of what you want at the output since boost converters only can supply voltages greater than a few volts above the supply and buck converters only can supply voltage at or below supply voltage ( minus diode voltage drops).

text:
This circuit is a linear converter, so if you try to use the circuit for higher current output then it will eventually heat up. Then you have to use any type of buck boost converter for controlling the motor speed. This circuit is good for 1A constant output. You can also use a circuit where 555 Timer is used for generating pwm pulses and it drives a n channel mosfet. And that mosfet is used for powering the motor. Specially here all current handling part is done by a mosfet. So it can handle much amps (5-10A).
Happy Building 😊
